description: The bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty terms across different medical specialties, comparing the performance of models fine-tuned on various specialty datasets. The horizontal axis represents six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, listed in a fixed order. The vertical axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and ranges from -27 to -22, with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 1. Each category on the horizontal axis is associated with a group of five bars, representing the negative log probability for models fine-tuned on Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, and Obstetrics/Pediatrics datasets, as indicated by the legend. The bars within each group are colored according to the fine-tuning dataset: light beige for Cardio, beige for Gastro, orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, and dark brown for Obstetrics/Pediatrics. The bars are grouped by category, with each group containing five bars of different colors. The height of the bars varies across categories and fine-tuning datasets, with the Cardio category showing the lowest negative log probability for the Cardio fine-tuned model at around -26.5, and the Neuro category showing the highest negative log probability for the Neuro fine-tuned model at around -22.8. The bars are not sorted in a specific order within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized. Overall, the chart provides a visual representation of how the negative log probability of per-specialty terms changes across different medical specialties and fine-tuning datasets.
